Updated verdict: ACCEPTUnder the repaired hypotheses, the all-phase joint-slot theorem and its proof are now mathematically coherent. The earlier objections are resolved by the exact final-model definitions:
$$P=\bigcup_i P_i,\qquad
M=\bigcup_i M_i,\qquad
T=\left(\bigcup_iT_i\right)\setminus P,$$
with no additional endpoints, no matching changes, and no degree-based reclassification of a  $T_j$ -site unless that site already lies in another source’s original  $P_i$ .I am accepting the theorem conditional on the stated established inputs: the exact ledger (1), the rotor barrier, the seven-of-twelve donor-ring injectivity result, and the stated rotor event-slot counts. The finite checker and Lean controls are not needed for the conclusion below.1. The repaired  $X_i$  predicate now supports the boundary tableThe important repair is that  $v$  is an intratile blank neighbor of  $p$ , while  $u$  is the other intratile neighbor of  $p$ , distinct from  $v$ . The reflected point is  $2p-u$ .With that definition, the phase catalogue is consistent for all even  $w\ge 6$  and even  $a,b\ge4$ :
$$\begin{array}{c|c|c|c}
\text{phase} & E_i & X_i & I_i\\
\hline
(0,0)&\varnothing&\varnothing&\varnothing\\
(0,1)&A&\varnothing&F,\ |I_i|=2\\
(1,0)&F&\varnothing&|I_i|=2w-2\\
(1,1)&F&A\cup F&|I_i|=2w-4.
\end{array}$$
The previously proposed phase- $(0,0)$  counterexample used  $u$  as another neighbor of the blank  $v$ , which is excluded by the repaired definition.The source-locality is also now correct.  $E_i$ ,  $X_i$ , and  $I_i$  are computed from the original support of source  $i$ , so endpoints belonging to another source do not incorrectly count as source- $i$  continuation endpoints.2. The marked-side endpoint argument is now validNormalize the positive source  $j$  as in the proof:
$$Q=\{2,3\}\times\{2,3\},$$
with
$$u=(2,2),\quad x=(3,2),\quad z=(2,3),\quad y=(3,3),$$
and positive endpoints
$$p=(3,1),\qquad q=(1,3),$$
together with protector blanks whose neighboring old blanks are  $u,v=(4,2),z$ .The repaired model makes the endpoint conclusion rigorous.If one of  $u,v,z$  becomes occupied, any source selection placed there would have both:its own source endpoint anchor, andthe adjacent positive endpoint protector.Therefore it would have at least two occupied neighbors and could not remain in final  $T$ . Optional extra selections cannot occupy these sites because they are required to have no endpoint neighbor. Hence a marked side forces at least one of  $u,v,z$  into final  $P$ .The coordinate correction regarding  $v$  is also decisive:  $v=(4,2)$  is directly adjacent to the old positive endpoint  $(4,1)$ . Thus the rule about newly occupied blanks adjacent to old endpoints applies to  $v$  exactly as it does to  $u$  and  $z$ .Gate occupiedSuppose  $u\in P$ , and let  $i$  be its unique original source owner. Since  $u$  was blank in the positive source  $j$ ,  $i\ne j$ .The only neighbors of  $u$  outside its physical tile are
$$(1,2)\quad\text{and}\quad(2,1),$$
and both belong to  $P_j$ . Since the original endpoint sets  $P_i$  are pairwise disjoint, neither belongs to  $P_i$ . Thus
$$u\in E_i.$$
The rotor barrier excludes a rotor owner, and the phase table therefore places  $u$  in one of the allowed phase- $(0,1)$  corner or phase- $(1,0)/(1,1)$  tip pools.Gate blankSuppose  $u\notin P$ . It cannot lie in final  $T$ , because it already has the two persistent positive endpoint neighbors  $(1,2)$  and  $(2,1)$ . Since final  $T$  is exactly  $(\bigcup_iT_i)\setminus P$ , this also implies that  $u$  was absent from every original source support.A marked side therefore has  $v\in P$  or  $z\in P$ .If  $v\in P$ , then  $x$  cannot remain in final  $T$ , because it would have occupied neighbors  $p$  and  $v$ . Since  $x\in T_j$  and final  $T$  is obtained only by deleting sites in  $P$ , this forces
$$x\in P.$$
Because  $x\notin P_j$ , its endpoint belongs to a different original source  $i$ . If instead  $z\in P$ , then  $z$  itself already has such a foreign original owner. Consequently, some
$$t\in\{x,z\}$$
belongs to  $P_i$  for  $i\ne j$ .This is the point at which the exact  $P=\bigcup_iP_i$  rule removes the prior promotion concern.  $x$  is not being arbitrarily reclassified as an endpoint of source  $j$ ; it can be in final  $P$  only because it is an original endpoint of another source.For  $t=x$ , the blank intratile neighbor is  $u$ , the other intratile neighbor is  $y$ , and
$$2x-y=(3,1)=p\in P_j.$$
For  $t=z$ ,
$$2z-y=(1,3)=q\in P_j.$$
Since  $P_i\cap P_j=\varnothing$ , the reflected point is not in  $P_i$ . Since  $u$  is blank in every source, it is absent from  $P_i\cup T_i$ . Therefore
$$t\in X_i.$$
The rotor barrier again excludes rotor ownership, and the phase table restricts the source to phase  $(1,1)$ , with  $t\in A_i\cup F_i$ .3. The side assignment is injectiveEach marked side is assigned one endpoint inside its positive donor tile  $Q$ .The established donor-ring result gives:all  $2N$  canonical donor tiles are distinct;the two canonical tiles within one positive source are distinct for  $w\ge6$ ;each donor tile has a seven-of-twelve original endpoint ring that prevents two owners from assigning the same endpoint.Therefore different marked sides receive different endpoint coordinates, even if the same foreign source witnesses several sides.The source-local boundary classification then places every assigned endpoint in its owner’s stated joint pool.4. The inactive-event argument now closes the only candidate overlapThe exact event definition is
$$K_{\mathrm{irregular}}
=
\sum_i
\left|
\left\{
p\in I_i:
\delta_i(p)\in P
\text{ and shares }p\text{’s physical tile}
\right\}
\right|.$$
Thus irregular events are endpoint-owned and cannot arise from an unrelated intertile contact.The candidate side pools and irregular pools are disjoint except for phase- $(1,1)$  upper corners  $A$ :phase  $(0,1)$ : side slots  $A$ , irregular slots  $F$ ;phase  $(1,0)$ : side slots  $F$ , with  $F\cap I_i=\varnothing$ ;phase  $(1,1)$ : side slots  $A\cup F$ , with  $F\cap I_i=\varnothing$  and  $A\subset I_i$ .A phase- $(1,1)$   $A$ -endpoint can only be assigned in the blank-gate case, so the gate  $u$  is final blank.It remains to verify that its unique original blank  $\delta_i(t)$  is exactly  $u$ . This follows from the physical tile geometry and the exact endpoint model:the  $A$ -endpoint has one intratile partner endpoint and one intratile blank;under the tiling-preserving isometry sending it to  $x$  or  $z$ , the partner must map either to  $y$  or to  $u$ ;it cannot map to  $u$ , because that partner is an element of  $P_i\subseteq P$ , while the gate case assumes  $u\notin P$ ;therefore the partner maps to  $y$ , and the unique blank maps to  $u$ .Hence
$$\delta_i(t)=u\notin P,$$
so the event at  $t$  does not occur. Any event at the partner endpoint is a distinct endpoint-owned event and is counted against its own slot in  $I_i$ ; it is not a reuse of the  $A$ -endpoint slot.Therefore the side-witness endpoints and irregular-event endpoints are genuinely disjoint.5. The slot count and density conclusion followThe available endpoint-slot capacities are
$$4B_{01}
+\sum_{\mathrm{phase}\,10}2w_i
+\sum_{\mathrm{phase}\,11}(2w_i-2)
+4R_{\mathrm{minus}}.$$
Using
$$S=B_{01}
+\sum_{\mathrm{phase}\,10}(w_i-1)
+\sum_{\mathrm{phase}\,11}(w_i-1)
+2R_{\mathrm{minus}},$$
this equals
$$2S+2B_{01}+2B_{10}.$$
The injective side assignment and endpoint-wise inactive-event argument therefore give
$$K_{\mathrm{irregular}}+G
\le
2S+2B_{01}+2B_{10}.
\tag{2}$$
Substituting into the established ledger inequality
$$\sigma\ge N+S+C-K_{\mathrm{irregular}}-G$$
yields
$$\sigma
\ge
N-S-2B_{01}-2B_{10}+C.
\tag{3}$$
Thus
$$N+C\ge S+2B_{01}+2B_{10}$$
is indeed sufficient for  $\sigma\ge0$ , and the width-expanded condition (5) follows.Final assessmentThe repaired theorem closes the defects identified in the first review: $X_i$  is now source-local and geometrically unambiguous; $v=(4,2)$  is correctly recognized as adjacent to the old endpoint  $(4,1)$ ;arbitrary  $T_j\to P_j$  promotion is excluded by the exact final rule  $P=\bigcup_iP_i$ ;any consumed  $x$ -site is necessarily an original endpoint of a foreign source;the irregular event is explicitly endpoint-owned and triggered only by the designated blank entering final  $P$ ;the phase- $(1,1)$   $A$ -corner overlap is inactive because its unique blank is forced to be the blank gate.I therefore update the earlier verdict from REVISE to ACCEPT for the stated complete source-fusion theorem. The result remains a sufficient condition for the declared fusion class, with the ledger and rotor barrier treated as the expressly established inputs; it does not assert necessity, sharpness, or an unrestricted theorem for arbitrary grid configurations.
